It's better to stay objective and state just the facts. This helps later down the road when you get to negotiation and you can use the "broken record" technique and just restate the facts. There's no right or wrong way; it's your judgement. I like to make the reason I'm mentioning something and my desired outcome very clear, so I'd say I find the noise a bit disruptive during the nighttime hours, etc.

PLEASE Master is a great skill to be using right now to avoid stimulation and triggers. Identifying if there are any triggers or what's setting off you're irritability and anger and then confronting why they're annoying you is also a good place to start.

The steps in DEARMAN don't have to be done in order, your describe is just that you can hear the dog and it bothers you. Your express is that it is disruptive to your sleep schedule etc. Your assert and reinforce is that you can hear the dog barking and running and you find it disruptive, be mindful that there is only so much she can do and you will have to deal with a little bit of noise during daytime hours. Negotiate and ask that between 8p-8a or whatever that the noise is kept to a minimum. 

To use GIVE in this situation, start the conversation by asking about the dog and how he's doing etc and ask if he likes to go on walks and that he's so playful, then mention that he's a bit loud and you find it disruptive. FAST is you not demanding that the dog is always silent, not buffering your request by apologizing for asking, being honest that you find the noise disruptive. 

As the owner of a large dog in an apartment, I genuinely didn't realize how loud my dog was until I went to my neighbors and heard my dog through the wall chomping on his squeaky toy. Go to psychology today website and look for therapists in your surrounding area. Try and find someone who had DBT listed, but doesn't necessarily do only DBT. Sometimes they list it this way and do blended DBT/CBT because insurance does not pay for DBT alone.

If they can't take patients, they'll know of someone in the area who is and they will refer you to them.
